entities.summary: Stephen Gerald Breyer is an American lawyer and jurist who served as an associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court from 1994 until his retirement in 2022. He was nominated by President Bill Clinton, and replaced retiring justice Harry Blackmun. Breyer was generally associated with the liberal wing of the Court. Since his retirement, he has been the Byrne Professor of Administrative Law and Process at Harvard Law School. Stephen Breyer was a writers & intellectuals from San Francisco (b. 1938-08-15, San Francisco). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a liberal justice on the US Supreme Court from 1994 to 2022, Stephen Breyer played a significant role in shaping American law and policy, particularly in areas such as civil rights, environmental protection, and campaign finance. His opinions have had a lasting impact on the country's legal landscape.
